newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates dip, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates dip, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates dipped on Tuesday as buying by spinners eased but dealers said speculation about a crop shortfall was likely to boost prices.
"The sharp rise in price resulted in oversupply and spinners slowing down their buying, hoping to get their requirements at lower rates," dealer Kishin Chand said.
But uncertainty about the size of the 1996/97 (July-June) crop was likely to push prices up in the next few days, he said.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,275 rupees ($56.56) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
